message: What scholarships are available for studying in Germany as a Kenyan?
expected_steps: 1. Identify matching programme (DAAD, KAS, IPS, Solitude), 2. Confirm language requirement (B2 minimum), 3. Check eligible countries list, 4. Prepare standard documents, 5. Apply via relevant portal
key_facts: DAAD STEM monthly stipend is €992. DAAD EPOS for development-related fields. KAS requires B2 German and social/political engagement. IPS pays €700/month for 4-week programme in Berlin.
policy_details: Most scholarships require B2 German minimum. DAAD does not cover tuition fees. KAS Kenya direct deadline: 1 March. IPS East Africa (Kenya) deadline: 15 May 2026 for IPS 2027.

message: How do I apply for the nursing apprenticeship programme in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm eligibility (B2 German + KCSE C + age 20-29), 2. Wait for application window (Jan or Jul), 3. Submit application via AG-Career Hub portal, 4. Take online aptitude test, 5. Attend preparation course at MKU, 6. Apply for training visa, 7. Arrive in Germany
key_facts: B2 German certificate must not be older than 1 year. KCSE minimum grade C. Age limit 20-29. Application opens January (for Sept/Oct start) and July (for April start). 54+ apprentices placed so far.
policy_details: SGAO programme partners: Hochschule Koblenz + Mount Kenya University + partner hospitals. Partner hospitals: Caritas Bad Mergentheim, Krankenhaus Tauberbischofsheim, Gemeinschaftsklinikum Mittelrhein (new from Oct 2025).

message: What are the requirements to study in Germany as a Kenyan student?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm KCSE grade C+ (undergraduate) or Bachelor's (postgraduate), 2. Determine language level needed (C1 German or A1/A2 for English programmes), 3. Prepare financial proof (block account or scholarship), 4. Choose programme and application route, 5. Apply for student visa
key_facts: KCSE C+ minimum for direct undergraduate admission. Block account €11,904 required (as of 2025). German C1 for German-taught programmes. A1/A2 for English-taught programmes. Application deadline Winter semester: 15 July.
policy_details: Block account amount (€11,904) updated annually — verify at German Embassy. Scholarships for undergraduate study are difficult to find. Uni-Assist charges application fees (~€75 first application).

message: What is WIDU.africa and how does it work for Kenyans in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm diaspora member (donor) lives in eligible European country, 2. Identify entrepreneur in Kenya or eligible African country, 3. Create WIDU account and invite entrepreneur, 4. Submit detailed investment plan, 5. Both parties make private investment first, 6. WIDU verifies investment, 7. Grant released after verification
key_facts: WIDU is a BMZ/GIZ initiative. Diaspora eligible countries: Germany, France, Switzerland, Austria, Netherlands, Norway, Belgium, Sweden. Entrepreneur eligible countries: Kenya, Ethiopia, Ghana, Cameroon, Togo, Tunisia. AG-Career Hub has been a WIDU partner since 2023.
policy_details: Private investment must be made and verified BEFORE grant is released. No partial payments. Equipment must be fully paid with private investment before WIDU verification. Filler budgets and consumable-heavy plans are common rejection reasons.

message: What should I do in the first weeks after arriving in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Register at Einwohnermeldeamt/Bürgeramt (within 2 weeks), 2. Receive Meldebescheinigung, 3. Wait for Steuer-ID to arrive by post (2-4 weeks), 4. Open German bank account, 5. Set up health insurance, 6. Join AG-Career Hub WhatsApp community
key_facts: Meldebescheinigung needed for bank account, phone contract, signing leases. Steuer-ID is sent automatically after Anmeldung — do NOT lose it. WhatsApp community has 1,400+ Kenyan professionals in Germany.
policy_details: Must register within 2 weeks of arrival. Landlord must provide Wohnungsgeberbestätigung — cannot register without it. Bürgeramt appointments in big cities (Munich, Berlin, Frankfurt) can be booked out 2-8 weeks — book immediately.

message: Are there job openings in Germany I can apply for right now?
expected_steps: 1. Check AG-Career Hub job listings, 2. Review Finance in Motion openings, 3. Check BASF internship programme, 4. Look at WTS tax advisory roles, 5. Contact socialbee for integration support
key_facts: Finance in Motion (Frankfurt) is hiring: HR Business Partner and Working Student roles. BASF Berufsorientierungspraktikum 2027 open (1-2 weeks, from 8th grade). WTS global tax firm has current openings at wts.com/karriere.
policy_details: Finance in Motion requires German B2 + English proficiency and German labour law knowledge for HR Business Partner role. BASF orientation internship requires no prior knowledge. WTS does not offer annual audits (independent firm).

message: What events does AG-Career Hub organise for Kenyans in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Describe 5th Career & Business Meet-up (June 28, 2025, Nürnberg), 2. Mention past events pattern, 3. Share community channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, YouTube), 4. Mention mentorship hub
key_facts: 5th Career & Business Networking Meet-up: 28 June 2025. Venue: TH Nürnberg Georg Simon Ohm, Bahnhofstraße 87, 90402 Nürnberg. Time: 10am-6pm plus evening programme. WhatsApp community has 1,400+ members.
policy_details: Tickets via Eventbrite. Children's corner available but SLOTS ARE LIMITED — must book in advance. Event is annual but city varies (past: Kronberg, Frankfurt, Nürnberg). Telegram channel also available.

message: How do I get a DAAD scholarship for STEM subjects as an African graduate?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm eligible country and completed Bachelor's degree, 2. Verify programme (DAAD STEM for developing/emerging countries), 3. Check language requirement (B2 German minimum), 4. Prepare application documents (form + motivation letter + references + transcripts), 5. Apply via DAAD scholarship database, 6. Attend digital interview if shortlisted
key_facts: DAAD STEM monthly stipend: €992. Duration: 10-24 months. Includes travel allowance, health insurance, annual study allowance €460. Must be from a developing or emerging country. Cannot apply if already have a Master's degree.
policy_details: DAAD does not cover tuition fees. Scholarship usually begins 1 October of following year. After year 1, academic progress is reviewed — scholarship continues only if on track. Language course (2-6 months) can be funded pre-programme if needed.

message: How can I invest in real estate in Kenya while living in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Consult AG-Career Hub Diaspora Investment Desk, 2. Contact property companies (Certified Homes, Optiven), 3. Review financing options, 4. Understand Kenyan property laws from diaspora
key_facts: Certified Homes Ltd (certifiedhomes.co.ke) and Optiven Limited (optiven.co.ke) are featured providers for Kenyan diaspora real estate. OBN Finance (obn-finance.com) advises on German real estate with diaspora context.
policy_details: Diaspora Investment Desk connects Kenyans with financial experts for both Kenya and Germany property. Real estate in Germany requires significant capital and is complex — OBN Finance combines mortgage calculations with a lawyer/tax consultant ecosystem.

message: How do I recognise my Kenyan law degree in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Understand that Kenyan law is NOT directly recognised in Germany, 2. Check anabin database (anabin.kmk.org) for your institution, 3. Get certified German translation of degree, 4. Pursue German Master's in International Business Law or related field, 5. Gain German legal language skills (C1), 6. Seek legal internship for practical exposure
key_facts: Kenyan law degree is NOT directly recognised as equivalent to German legal qualifications. Angella Kerubo case study: Steinbeis University Berlin Master's in International Business Law (2016-2018) → career in data privacy. Anabin database rates institutions H+, H+-, or H-.
policy_details: Best pathway: German Master's (LLM or International Business Law) + C1 German + data privacy/GDPR specialisation. ZAB Statement of Comparability costs ~€200, takes 4-8 weeks. Certified translation of degree: €50-150 per document.

message: What is the KAS scholarship and how do I apply from Kenya?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm eligibility (B2 German, academic excellence, social/political engagement), 2. Choose degree type (Master's or PhD at German university), 3. For Kenya direct application: Send to Ms. Eva-Maria Okot by 1 March 2026, 4. For domestic (already in Germany) application: Apply via campus.kas.de by 15 July
key_facts: KAS targets: Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Ethiopia (East Africa office). Benefits include: financial support + international network (15,000+ alumni) + seminar programme + personal mentoring. Deadline in Germany: 15 July noon CET each year via campus.kas.de.
policy_details: Kenya/East Africa direct application deadline: 1 March 2026. KAS looks for positive attitude toward democracy, pluralism, and human rights. Excellent academic performance required. Programme funded by Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung e.V.

message: What German language level do I need for nursing in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm B2 is the minimum required, 2. Specify certificate must be ≤1 year old, 3. Explain accepted certificates (Goethe-Institut, telc), 4. Mention preparation course at MKU covers medical German, 5. Advise on timeline to reach B2
key_facts: B2 is the minimum for nursing apprenticeship (SGAO programme). Certificate must not be older than 1 year. Goethe-Institut B2 is most widely accepted. Timeline from zero to B2: approximately 12-18 months of study.
policy_details: Medical German terminology is covered in the preparation course at MKU. Goethe-Institut Nairobi is the main exam centre in Kenya — book 2-3 months in advance. After B2 for nursing, C1 is needed for career advancement in Germany.

message: I have a KCSE grade of C+ — can I study in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm C+ meets undergraduate eligibility requirement, 2. Assess language situation (German or English programme), 3. Identify financial proof requirement (block account €11,904), 4. Guide through course selection (DAAD database, Hochschulkompass), 5. Explain application process (direct or Uni-Assist)
key_facts: KCSE C+ meets the minimum requirement for direct undergraduate admission. Block account €11,904 required (2025). English-taught programmes require only A1/A2 German. German-taught programmes require C1 German.
policy_details: C (plain) KCSE does NOT meet undergraduate study requirement (only nursing programme). C+ or above required for direct study admission. Studienkolleg is an option for students below C+. Scholarships for undergraduate study are difficult to find — block account is more reliable route.

message: How do I get from a B1 German level to B2 for the nursing programme?
expected_steps: 1. Explain B2 is required and certificate must be ≤1 year, 2. Estimate 4-6 months additional study from B1, 3. Recommend Goethe-Institut preparation course and exam, 4. Mention medical German additional preparation at MKU
key_facts: From B1 to B2 takes approximately 4-6 months of consistent study (10-15 hours/week). Goethe-Institut Nairobi is the main exam centre in Kenya. Intensive courses can halve the timeline.
policy_details: Certificate for SGAO nursing must not be older than 1 year at time of application. Goethe-Institut exam in Nairobi — book 2-3 months in advance as slots fill quickly. The SGAO preparation course at MKU covers medical German but requires B2 first.

message: What support does AG-Career Hub offer for settling in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Registration guidance (Anmeldung process), 2. Bank account options (N26, Sparkasse), 3. Health insurance providers (Barmer, SBK — AG-Career Hub partners), 4. WhatsApp community (1,400+ members), 5. Events and networking (annual meetup)
key_facts: AG-Career Hub WhatsApp community: 1,400+ Kenyan professionals in Germany. Barmer (barmer.de) and SBK (sbk.org) are AG-Career Hub sponsor partners with English support. Fintiba (fintiba.com) handles blocked account + health insurance together. LEMFI for cross-border transfers.
policy_details: SBK offers English-language support for expats: sbk.org/sbk-en/expats-english-careerhub. WhatsApp community requires small subscription fee. Telegram channel is free. 5th meetup on 28 June 2025 in Nürnberg for networking.

message: What are the options for Kenyans who want to become freelancers or self-employed in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Explain freiberuflich vs gewerblich distinction, 2. Mention Institut für Freie Berufe (IFB) as key advisor, 3. Explain Gewerbeanmeldung vs Freiberufler registration, 4. Note tax registration requirements, 5. Mention Allan Onsando (WTS) for tax aspects
key_facts: Institut für Freie Berufe (IFB) at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg is Germany's leading advisor for freelancers (freie-berufe.com). Julia Miller, Head of Start-up Consulting at IFB, presented at the 5th AG-Career Hub event on self-employment in Germany.
policy_details: Freelance (freiberuflich) professions include: scientific, artistic, writing, teaching, educational fields. Trade business (Gewerbe) has additional registration requirements. Side business (Nebengewerbe) is possible alongside employment. IFB advisory contact: freie-berufe.com.

message: What is the Bundestag IPS scholarship and who can apply?
expected_steps: 1. Explain the 4-week Berlin programme structure, 2. State eligibility (under 30, East Africa: Kenya/Tanzania/Uganda, B2 German, university degree), 3. Describe application process (IPS digital platform), 4. State application window (1 April – 15 May 2026 for IPS 2027), 5. Mention €700 monthly stipend
key_facts: Bundestag IPS: Up to 24 scholars from 9 sub-Saharan countries. €700/month stipend + free accommodation + travel costs + insurance. Programme runs 4 weeks (Jan 4 – Feb 2, 2027 for IPS 2027 cohort). Core: 1-week internship in a Bundestag member's office.
policy_details: Application via 'IPS digital' platform only (not email anymore). Deadline for IPS 2027: 1 April – 15 May 2026. Under 30, B2 German, completed university studies, strong political/social commitment required. Motivation letter must be in German, hand-signed, max 2 pages.

message: How does the 360 Labour Mobility Programme help Kenyans find jobs in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Explain the 360° concept (comprehensive support for qualified workers), 2. Name the founder (Edith Otiende-Lawani, GAaNF Munich), 3. Describe services (job matching, integration support, legal guidance), 4. Mention target sectors (healthcare, engineering, law), 5. Connect to Germany-Kenya Labour Mobility Agreement (Sept 2024)
key_facts: 360° Labour Mobility Programme is one of 15 expert institutions for Germany's skills shortage. Founded by Edith Otiende-Lawani (Lawyer, GAaNF e.V.). Started with Ghana and Nigeria; expanding to Kenya. Connects skilled job seekers with German employers.
policy_details: Germany-Kenya Labour Mobility Agreement signed 13 September 2024 — Kenya was first African country to sign such agreement with Germany. The agreement focuses on win-win: labour migration to Germany AND local job creation, outsourcing, skills transfer.

message: Can I do an internship at BASF in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Describe BASF Berufsorientierungspraktikum 2027, 2. State duration (1-2 weeks), 3. List available fields (chemistry, IT, engineering, business), 4. Explain application process (no prior knowledge needed), 5. Mention it is for students from 8th grade onwards
key_facts: BASF Berufsorientierungspraktikum 2027: 1-2 weeks, at Ludwigshafen am Rhein. No prior knowledge required. Available from 8th grade. Fields include: chemistry, IT, biology, engineering, business, mechatronics.
policy_details: Apply via BASF jobs portal: basf.jobs/BASF_Azubi. For 2027 internship, apply now via the online button on the posting page. School report (Zeugnis) required — no cover letter or CV needed. Contact: BASF SE, Ludwigshafen, applications@basf.com.

message: What career paths have Kenyans built in Germany in the IT and engineering sector?
expected_steps: 1. List IT professionals from community (James Kimathi, Faith Njuguna, John Waweru, Brian Saa), 2. Describe engineering paths (Kelvin Makaka, Noel Sanya), 3. Mention Africa Kommt fellowship (SAP), 4. Suggest erp4students for SAP skills, 5. Refer to AG-Career Hub events for networking
key_facts: James Kimathi: Senior Tech Lead at DocMorris, SAP expertise. Faith Njuguna: Electrical/Electronics Engineer at ALTEN GmbH. John Waweru: GIS/Data Science at Bezirksregierung Köln via DAAD scholarship from Bonn University. Brian Saa: SAP Team Lead at Computacenter via Afrika Kommt fellowship.
policy_details: erp4students (erp4students.de) offers SAP S/4HANA certification courses — university accredited. Peter Dianga case: DAAD Leadership for Africa + erp4students → logistics job in Bremen. AG-Career Hub 5th meetup features IT/engineering speakers.

message: What is the Akademie Schloss Solitude fellowship and who can apply?
expected_steps: 1. Describe the fellowship (residential, Stuttgart), 2. State benefits (€1,200/month + free studio), 3. Explain eligibility (artists, scientists, cultural professionals; not undergrads), 4. List practice areas (visual, music, digital, architecture, literature, etc.), 5. Mention selection cycle (every 2 years, max 65 fellows)
key_facts: Akademie Schloss Solitude: €1,200/month grant + free furnished studio including electricity, water, heating + travel expenses. Fellowship duration: 6, 9, or 12 months. Must be physically in Stuttgart minimum 2/3 of fellowship period. Selection rounds every 2 years.
policy_details: Enrolled undergraduate students cannot apply — PhD students may apply. Must register permanent residence in Stuttgart. Families/partners cannot always be accommodated (especially from abroad due to entry/residence regulations). Application: akademie-solitude.de.

message: What preparation course must I do before the nursing apprenticeship in Germany?
expected_steps: 1. Explain preparation course is at Mount Kenya University (MKU), 2. List what is covered (intercultural training, medical German, basic nursing, German healthcare system), 3. Explain what happens simultaneously (visa processing), 4. Describe German partner support on arrival
key_facts: Preparation course is held at Mount Kenya University (MKU). Content: intercultural training, medical German terminology, basic nursing skills, German healthcare system overview. Visa application documents are processed during the preparation course period.
policy_details: The preparation course is part of the SGAO project structure. German partner hospitals assist with visa interviews and airport pickup after course completion. Preparation course fees are not publicly documented — contact AG-Career Hub or MKU directly for current costs.

message: I have KCSE C+, I'm 23, my German is currently B1, and I want to be in Germany within 18 months — what's the fastest realistic path?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm B1 → B2 takes 4-6 months so B2 achievable in 5-6 months, 2. Apply to SGAO July window (for April start) once B2 achieved, 3. KCSE C+ meets nursing requirement (C plain needed so C+ qualifies), 4. Age 23 is within 20-29 window, 5. After acceptance: preparation course at MKU, visa, arrival Germany, 6. On arrival: Anmeldung within 2 weeks + bank account + Steuer-ID by post
key_facts: B2 takes 4-6 months from B1. SGAO applications open January (for Sept/Oct) and July (for April). KCSE C+ qualifies (C minimum needed). Age 23 is within 20-29 range. 54+ apprentices placed across 4 cohorts.
policy_details: B2 certificate must not be older than 1 year at application time. Book Goethe-Institut exam 2-3 months in advance. SGAO portal opens twice yearly — user must time B2 achievement with the application window.

message: I'm a Kenyan lawyer with 5 years experience — my degree isn't recognised in Germany. What are ALL my options and which worked best for others?
expected_steps: 1. Confirm Kenyan law degree is NOT directly recognised as German legal qualification, 2. Explain the documented pathway: German Master's in International Business Law (Steinbeis Berlin), 3. Emphasise C1 German needed + legal terminology + internship at German law firm, 4. Share Angella Kerubo outcome: Data Privacy career at NIO/Fresenius, 5. Mention WTS for tax/legal careers, Angella Onsomu (Fresenius) as second case study, 6. Check anabin for institution rating
key_facts: Angella Kerubo: Kenyan law → Steinbeis University Berlin Master's in International Business Law 2016-2018 → Privacy Counsel at NIO. Angella Onsomu: Senior Data Privacy Expert at Fresenius Medical Care. C1 German required. ZAB Statement of Comparability: ~€200, 4-8 weeks.
policy_details: German law degree (Erste/Zweite Juristische Prüfung) is the protected German legal qualification — foreign degrees cannot substitute directly. Data Privacy/GDPR is a highly effective niche for Kenyan lawyers in Germany combining both legal backgrounds.

message: I want to support a small chicken farm in Kenya through WIDU.africa but my entrepreneur's investment plan was rejected — what went wrong and how do I fix it?
expected_steps: 1. Diagnose likely rejection reasons (consumable-heavy, out-of-order steps, filler budget, over/under-quoting), 2. Explain the correct sequence: build coop BEFORE buying chicks, 3. Private investment must be made and FULLY verified before grant released, 4. Focus on infrastructure not stock (chicks are consumable), 5. Rewrite plan with strategic asset allocation, realistic market prices, sustainability plan, 6. Watch AG-Career Hub WIDU webinar for examples
key_facts: Common WIDU rejection reasons: consumable-heavy plans (chicks/food), out-of-order steps (chicks before coop), filler budgets, over/under-quoting. No partial payments — full private investment must be verified before grant. Equipment and assets must be fully paid with private funds first.
policy_details: WIDU grant released AFTER verification of private investment — not before. Building a chicken coop should come BEFORE purchasing chicks. Coaches look for: strategic allocation, efficiency, sustainability (3-6 months without another round), scalability beyond local village. AG-Career Hub has been WIDU partner since 2023 and can advise.
